item.title: Texas women's basketball: Longhorns roll past Southeastern Louisiana to a 7-0 start
item.description: Isi Etute of the Texas Longhorns looks to pass the ball while defended by Lucia Navarro of the Tarleton State Texans during the second half Nov. 14, 2026 at Moody Center in Austin. (Scott Wachter/Getty Images) This Thanksgiving, the Texas women's basketball team can be thankful for an undefeated start to its season. Texas got double-digit point totals from six different players in Wednesday's 96-45 win over Southeastern Louisiana at Moody Center. With the win, the sixth-ranked Longhorns improved to 7-0 against a schedule that has featured four opponents that qualified for the 2026 NCAA Tournament. More: Subscribe to the Statesman's Texas sports newsletter Texas has yet to trail in a game this season, and the Longhorns weren't in danger of facing that first deficit on Wednesday night. Fueled by an early 15-0 run, Texas seized a 23-5 lead by the end of the first quarter and took a 34-point lead into halftime. A Southland Conference representative, Southeastern Louisiana (2-5) trailed by as many as 55 points in the second half. Sophomore guard Jayda Clark and freshman forward Isi Etute respectively scored 19 and 18 points to lead the Longhorns. Texas also got 14 points, 10 assists and six steals from All-American forward Madison Booker . Starting guard Zya Vann missed Wednesday's action with an undisclosed injury. According to a team spokesperson, Vann is expected back by Sunday's road game at Southeast Missouri State. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, McCarthy has completed 56.1% of his passes traveling 10 or more air yards this season — a rate topped by only two qualified quarterbacks, Joe Burrow (70.2%) and Trevor Lawrence (58.2%). Over that same stretch, the Colts have allowed an average of 239 passing yards and two passing touchdowns per game to opposing quarterbacks. item.description: OKLAHOMA CITY — As the final seconds ticked away, Kenrich Williams had a chance to make it a one-point deficit with seconds to go. After missing, Ajay Mitchell had the same chance. He also missed from the outside. The two most consequential shots of the night once again fell short. The Oklahoma City Thunder didn't have enough fourth-quarter firepower in their 113-106 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves . This was part of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B play. Changing up the starters once again, the Thunder couldn't solve their slow starts. They were in a 26-16 deficit after the first quarter. Offense continued to be a problem for short-handed OKC as it fell behind by double-digit points. Fueled by Alex Caruso's defensive energy, the second unit did a lot better to open the second frame. The Thunder exploded for 37 points in the second frame. Quite the juxtaposition from the opening frame. That included a 20-8 run. Gilgeous-Alexander drilled a stepback 3-pointer on Jaden McDaniels' grill. Caruso took on LaMelo Ball as the primary defender to gum up Minnesota's fast-paced offense. After such a strong second quarter, the Thunder had a 53-47 halftime lead over the Timberwolves. All things considered, that was a great spot to be at. Minnesota has been one of the hottest teams since Anthony Edwards went down with knee surgery. Meanwhile, OKC has been reeling with a ton of similar-looking losses piling up. Like usual, the wheels started falling off for the Thunder in the second half. Ball went on a heater with circus-looking jumpers. OKC's once-indestructible defense looked mortal. Actually, scratch that — detrimental. The Timberwolves ballooned for 40 points in the third frame. That made OKC's 30-point frame an afterthought. McDaniels' buzzer-beating heave that swished in was the excruciating cherry on top. The Thunder were in an 87-83 deficit after the third quarter. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The Houston Rockets picked up an impressive 116-104 victory over the Phoenix Suns , but the star of the show was Alperen Sengun . The Houston big man delivered a historic performance with 23 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists, recording a triple-double while passing Hakeem Olajuwon in the franchise record books (2nd in franchise history in triple-doubles). It was another reminder of how special Sengun has become in the best season of his career so far. Sengun wasn’t alone, though. Kevin Durant finished with 20 points and 10 rebounds, while Amen Thompson added 18 points, 10 rebounds, and four assists. Jabari Smith Jr. and Fred VanVleet contributed 13 points apiece, giving Houston five starters in double figures. The Rockets controlled the glass, winning the rebounding battle 51-38 and collecting 20 offensive rebounds. They also moved the ball effectively, finishing with 30 assists. Phoenix struggled badly from the perimeter, making just 5-32 three-point attempts (15.6%), which made it difficult to keep pace despite Devin Booker ‘s 25 points and Jalen Green ‘s 16-point contribution from the backcourt. Houston’s biggest concern was its free-throw shooting. The Rockets made just 16-30 attempts, leaving plenty of points at the line. Fortunately, their rebounding advantage, balanced scoring, and Sengun’s historic night were enough to secure the 12-point victory. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LOS ANGELES – When the Los Angeles Lakers began the 2026-27 season, Ziaire Williams was penciled in as one of the team’s starting forwards. He started out the year in a nice rhythm through the first four games before sustaining a foot injury . He was then sidelined for three games, and since making his return, he’s alternated with Jake LaRavia between starting and coming off the bench. Since returning to the Lakers’ lineup, Ziaire Williams’ shooting rhythm from 3-point range hasn’t quite been as efficient as it was to begin the season. There hasn’t been a huge drop-off, but it’s been ever so slightly noticeable. It can be a bit of a challenge for a player who has been out to get back into a consistent rhythm after not playing in a while. For Williams, part of it just boils down to accepting the role he is in. “I feel like I’m in rhythm. The role I have, some games I might get two shots, some games I might get 10. It just depends on if the ball finds me,” Williams said following Lakers’ practice last Sunday. “I’m cool with that. I’m just trying to do whatever I can to impact winning. item.title: 'We needed to take that risk!' - Bruno Fernandes reveals half-time tactical switch behind Manchester United's Lisbon turnaround
item.description: TOPSHOT-FBL-EUR-C1-SPORTING-MAN UTD - AFP Bruno Fernandes inspired a fierce second-half turnaround with two goals in three minutes as Manchester United drew 2-2 away to Sporting CP in the Champions League. Named Player of the Match, the United skipper explained how aggressive pressing rattled Sporting after half-time before late drama denied Mauricio Pochettino his first win. Fernandes leads United's rapid second-half response Bruno Fernandes dragged Manchester United back from a frustrating first half with two goals inside three minutes after the interval, though Mauricio Pochettino had to settle for a 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP. Trailing to Luis Suarez's 33rd-minute penalty after Amad Diallo's header was ruled out for a foul by Youri Tielemans, United struck back through Fernandes' 48th-minute spot-kick and a deflected long-range strike two minutes later. "I wanted to win the game. It was very important for us to win because of our position in the Champions League, but it was also important not to lose," Fernandes told UEFA after receiving the Player of the Match award. "It's very tough to play here at Alvalade, with the great atmosphere created by the fans and a very good team." Explaining the high-pressing shift against Paulo Fonseca's side United struggled to break down Sporting's high defensive line before the interval, with Joshua Zirkzee firing off target on his first start since May and Bryan Mbeumo crowded out. However, Fernandes revealed a bolder pressing approach after the break transformed the contest. "We came back very strong in the game because we could put some intensity into pressing high. We need to take that risk sometimes, playing one-on-one and having more people in front," he explained. "As Sporting want to play from the back, sometimes when you are very aggressive, you can recover some balls and get into a good position." Late errors, VAR heartbreak and a fair verdict Fernandes nearly completed a quickfire hat-trick when a free-kick flew just wide, before goalkeeper Senne Lammens spilled Ivan Fresneda's 80th-minute cross to gift Suarez an equaliser. United saw a late Kaique own goal disallowed by VAR for a foul and lost Tielemans to a second yellow card in stoppage time. Reflecting on Paulo Fonseca's tactical setup, Fernandes admitted a share of the spoils was justified: "The way Paulo Fonseca set his team up against us was different. We knew they would play a high line, which forced them to take risks, but at the same time made it difficult for us to reach the final third and get the ball in behind. Overall, I think it was a very good game, and the draw was a fair result." United sit 19th as Pochettino searches for first victory Having suffered defeat at Anfield on Sunday before Wednesday's chaotic stalemate in Lisbon, Pochettino remains in search of his maiden victory as Manchester United manager. item.title: 'Maybe I need to move here!' - Anthony Gordon jokes about relocating to Azerbaijan after firing Champions League brace for Barcelona against Sabah FK
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-SABAH-BARCELONA - AFP Anthony Gordon ended his month-long goal drought with a clinical brace as Barcelona defeated Sabah FK in the Champions League at the Baku Olympic Stadium. Having now scored six goals across two Champions League visits to Azerbaijan, the England forward joked he might need to relocate there while admitting he should have claimed a hat-trick. Gordon ends goal drought with clinical brace in Baku Anthony Gordon fired two goals to help Barcelona justify their status as heavy favourites with a commanding Champions League victory over Sabah FK at the Baku Olympic Stadium. Having won the starting spot on the left wing ahead of Karim Adeyemi since arriving last summer, the England international finally added end product to his high-intensity pressing by striking in the 30th and 50th minutes—capitalising on rebounds from goalkeeper Pokatilov on both occasions while seeing another effort disallowed after a VAR review. Having last scored for Barcelona against Alaves on October 31, Gordon joked about his remarkable affinity for Azerbaijan after netting four times there for Newcastle United against Qarabag last season. "Maybe at some point in my life I need to move here! I've been very successful here, and yeah, great game today. Obviously two goals, so I'm happy, but potentially could have had a hat-trick, so still a lot of work to do," Gordon told Stan . Missing a hat-trick and overcoming a gruelling journey Asked after full-time whether six goals in two seasons made him the "King of Baku", Gordon played down the title while ruing a missed left-footed chance for a treble. He also praised Barcelona's collective focus after a long trip away from home. "I wouldn't say that, but it's a very special place for me. I should have scored a hat-trick, but I missed that one with my left foot. I'm very happy," he explained. Reflecting on the squad's display, Gordon added: "I think it was very good because, like I said, it's really difficult to travel. We came here two days ago to come away from family and have this kind of experience, but Azerbaijan is a beautiful place." Chasing Harry Kane's English Champions League benchmark Gordon's double lifted his tally to three goals in five Champions League appearances this season, having also netted against Galatasaray. Across his career, he now boasts 13 goals in his first 23 Champions League proper outings—a record among English players surpassed only by Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane, who scored 18 in his first 23 appearances. For the next 17 weeks, I will produce weekly fantasy content that will go over the waiver wire, rankings, and Start 'Em, Sit 'Em columns. Being a fantasy manager often means having to make difficult roster decisions, but I aim to take some of the guesswork out of it with my Start 'Em and Sit 'Em column for every position. item.description: Explained: Why MI purse value has been reduced ahead of IPL 2027 mini-auction originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mumbai Indians ' auction purse has dropped by ₹2.35 crore, from ₹32.60 crore to ₹30.25 crore. The revision is linked to retention-slot valuation after Hardik Pandya's departure. MI's four retained capped players have a combined slab value of ₹61 crore, above their actual salaries. MI will enter the IPL 2027 mini-auction with ₹30.25 crore and nine slots to fill. Explained: Why MI's IPL 2027 auction purse reduced by ₹2.35 crore after BCCI revision The Mumbai Indians' purse for the upcoming IPL 2027 mini-auction has been cut down to ₹30.25 crore due to the revision of the purse value by the BCCI. The five-time champions were initially allotted ₹32.60 crore after the retention and release list , but their revised purse value in the mini-auction was declared to be ₹30.25 crore on November 25 . This revision in purse has led to confusion among the people regarding the reason behind such an occurrence since all the nine other teams have retained their purse values from the time of their retention and release list. MORE: IPL 2027 auction player pool: Initial register, overseas players and deadline Why has Mumbai Indians' purse been reduced by ₹2.35 crore? This reduction is related to the valuation of MI's retained players under the IPL's retention-slot rule, in light of Hardik Pandya's transfer to Punjab Kings (PBKS). Initially, Mumbai used the sum total of the salaries of the four remaining capped players that are, Jasprit Bumrah, Rohit Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav and Tilak Varma. The salaries of the aforementioned players are ₹18 crore, ₹16.30 crore, ₹16.35 crore and ₹8 crore, respectively, which adds up to ₹58.65 crore. But the IPL's retention rule requires teams to consider the cost of retention slots for the players, as opposed to simply adding up the salary cost of the players. Accordingly, with respect to the new calculation rule, the four retained capped players of MI have been evaluated at ₹61 crore. Consequently, the difference between the two valuations comes out to be ₹2.35 crore. The difference arises because the comparison is done between the salary of four retained capped players of Mumbai and their respective retention-slot value. item.description: With just one regular-season game remaining, Illinois coach Bret Bielema is already looking toward what could be a very busy offseason. The Fighting Illini are about to close out their regular season Saturday against Northwestern in Evanston, but questions surrounding their roster, injuries and the program’s future are already beginning. Keeping the offensive line together While the transfer portal continues to change the landscape of college football, Bielema made it clear that keeping his current players in Champaign will be a major offseason priority. “Obviously, the number one name of the game for us is retention,” Bielema said. One position group Bielema is particularly focused on is the offensive line, which could return all five starters next season. “In theory, you know, we would have the potential to have all five offensive linemen return, right?” Bielema said. A major part of that possibility centers around center Jake Renfro, who has another year of eligibility available after receiving a waiver from the NCAA. Renfro, who started his career at Cincinnati during the 2019-20 season, may now have the ability to play in 2026-27. “His waiver came back with two years,” Bielema said. “So, he has this year and another year.” Bielema said he plans to meet with Renfro following the season to discuss his future with the program. The veteran coach also praised Renfro’s physical abilities, comparing him to former NFL centers Travis Frederick and Frank Ragnow, both of whom Bielema previously coached. However, keeping the offensive line intact won’t necessarily be easy. Bielema said he plans to begin meeting individually with players shortly after the Northwestern game, with offensive linemen expected to be among his first conversations. “The months of December and January are probably the most intense months now as a coach that have nothing to do with football,” Bielema said. Injuries continue to pile up While retaining players is a major concern for next season, simply keeping players healthy has become an equally difficult challenge for Illinois. Bielema revealed Monday that nearly a quarter of the roster has been sidelined by injuries in recent weeks. “For us in the last two weeks of the season, I believe we’re at 24 players that can’t practice or play,” Bielema said. The offense has taken the brunt of the force this season in regard to injuries. Now, wide receiver Ty Robinson and tight end Kaden Feagin will also be out on Saturday. “We’ve significantly changed and scaled back the number of reps we have during practice,” Bielema said. “It’s always a balancing act at the end of the year, but this year more than ever.” One player whose availability remains uncertain is quarterback Katin Houser, who returned against Iowa after clearing concussion protocol late last week. “He’s definitely a guy that’s a warrior,” Bielema said. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? Beaten 3-0 at home and reduced to 10 men in the 36th minute, Miami could even have lost their Argentine captain just before halftime after a moment of petulance. As he prepared to take a throw-in, Lionel Messi threw the ball straight at the head of Gonzalo Tapia, who scored twice on the night for Columbus Crew. Despite this uncharacteristic act from Lionel Messi, the referee decided to show La Pulga only a yellow card. Many spectators felt the punishment was too lenient, believing Miami's number 10 should have been sent off. Whatever the case, the Florida club face an uphill battle to reach the next round of the playoffs, with a three-goal deficit to overturn away at Columbus Crew next Saturday. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
